SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE
APPLICATION NUMBER 23024-T1

17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans — 2137-47 West Irving Park Road, Chicago. IL

Proposed Zoning: B3-3 Community Shopping District
Lot Area: 17,750 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to develop the subject property with a new four-
story mixed-use building containing a parking garage and approximately
4,545 sq. ft. of retail space at grade, twenty-four (24) dwelling units above,
and a roof top deck. The proposed building will measure 65 ft. in height.
The subject property is a Transit Served Location and will be supported by
twenty-four (24) off-street garage parking spaces and fifty-four (54) onsite
bicycle parking spaces. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-0303-D optional
Administrative Adjustment and Variation and pursuant to Secs. 17-13-
1003-EE and 17-13-1101-B of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the
Applicant is seeking to increase the residential off-street parking ratio from
50% (12 parking spaces) to 100% (24 parking spaces), reduce the rear
setback for floors containing residential units from 30 ft. to 3.5 in., and is
seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Chicago Zoning code, for the
attached plans. Please note the Applicant will provide two (2) on-site
affordable units at 30% AMI to meet its obligation under the Affordable
Requirements Ordinance (Option 4 - 10% ata weighted average of 30% of

the AMI).

(A) _ The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 50,735 square feet (2.86 FAR)

(B) _ The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 739.5 square feet
(24 residential units proposed)

(C) The amount of off-street parking: 24 parking spaces

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location based on its
proximity to the Irving Park CTA Bus Route. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-BE, the
Applicant is seeking to increase the off-street parking ratio from 50% (12 parking

spaces) to 100% (24 parking spaces).

(D) Setbacks:
a. Front Setback: 1.5 inches

b. Side Setbacks:

West Side: zero

East Side: 3.5 inches
c. Rear Setback: 6 inches

Final for Publication

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the rear setback
for floors containing residential units from 30 feet to 3.5 inches.

(E) Building Height: 65 feet

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 217 linear feet of the Irving Park CTA Bus
Route. The proposed mixed-use building containing retail space at grade and twenty-four
(24) residential units above will be supported by twenty-four(24) off-street parking spaces.
Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to increase the residential off-
street parking ratio from 50% (12 parking spaces) to 100% (24 parking spaces).

2. The Applicant’s building design complies with the requirements of Sec. 17-4-0504 because
the residential entrance and the retail portion of the proposed building fronts along West
Irving Park Road. The building’s first floor is designed with widows facing the sidewalk
along Irving Park Road and the building’s proposed front setback is 3.5 inches.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Irving Park CTA Bus Route. The Applicant believes the development
will improve the subject area for residents and other commuters traveling in the subject

area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain a grade-level retail space and parking
garage, and twenty-four (24) residential units above, and a roof top deck. The proposed
building will be supported by twenty-four (24) off-street garage parking spaces and fifty-
four (54) onsite bicycle parking spaces. The Applicant is seeking administrative approval
to permit the off-street parking ratio (24 parking spaces proposed) for the residential units
pursuant to the TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace a commercial
building witha surface parking lot and a two-story mixed-use building and detached garage
with a new mixed-use building offering new retail space along West Irving Park Road.
The proposed residential units will provide additional residential housing inventory tomeet
market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to mass transit, the Applicant
believes the project provides transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel
Demand Study and Management Plan rules promulgated by the Department of
Transportation by serving an area in need.
